## Active continuation — PR head `2cee3d2`

PR #2 is OPEN/Draft at `2cee3d20ac036dd1f368cbc1b558feed3529fa5f` (`REVIEW_REQUIRED`, merge blocked). Push run [40588470046](https://github.com/ramajittilearn-ctrl/ERP-TakyApartment/actions/runs/40588470046) passed all five jobs; PR run [40588478879](https://github.com/ramajittilearn-ctrl/ERP-TakyApartment/actions/runs/40588478879) failed container verification after the other four jobs passed. The PR binary report identifies GO-2026-6860 (`html.Parse`/`ParseFragment`) and GO-2026-6866 (`html.Render`) in x/net v0.60.0, fixed in v0.62.0; the prior push scan of the same binary did not show them. The Go database index currently reports `2026-10-21T00:27:29Z`, older than the two official advisory records (`2026-10-27T21:16:18Z`), so local clean scans against that index cannot clear the findings.

Parallel implementation is underway in isolated branch `codex/phase4-security-builds-20261028`: rclone dependency/build/source-scan parity and the same-run authenticated provenance-to-libxml2-candidate path. Independent cross-review exchanged actionable findings and corrections; reviewer confirmation of the final base-image ID assertion is pending. Exact-head hosted CI remains required. The first push run 40605155752 failed lint on four consumer globals/regex issues and the candidate artifact step ran after prerequisite jobs were skipped; both causes were fixed in `e28ed36` and that exact run passed quality, provenance and Stage 5; its candidate artifact materialization failed on numeric `run_attempt` comparison and upstream orig-tarball naming. Both were reproduced against its real artifact and fixed locally; the consumer now validates all 44 files. The hosted candidate build ran on 2b62d08 and failed at APT TLS validation inside Docker because the builder did not trust the runner CA; same-run artifact materialization and provenance succeeded. A reviewed BuildKit secret-mount correction is implemented locally, preserves signed repository checks, restores trust bundle before layer success, and records only its hash; independent review and hosted rerun remain pending. Agent UAT 90/90 and Stage 5 52 checks/17 migrations already passed on the current code head; repeat only if changes affect those behaviors. Raw database scans still show Bookworm 2 Critical/66 High and Trixie 1 Critical/61 High. No patched package/image, publication, merge, production deployment or Owner UAT acceptance is evidenced. Production remains NO-GO.

New supplemental scratch evidence (not yet CI-integrated): SHA-256-pinned official GO-2026-6860/6866 JSON records were placed in a small local diagnostic overlay. Against the same overlay, baseline rclone/x/net v0.60.0 reports GO-2026-6860 with a reachable `backend/http.ReadDir → html.Parse` trace; the x/net v0.62.0 source reports no findings. This proves the parser path and supports the fixed dependency, but does not yet prove GO-2026-6866 source reachability, exact production binary remediation, or the full canonical vulnerability state. Keep all full scans and raw Trivy gates.

## Open gates before any production cutover
1. The exact production host, Docker context, Compose project, canonical HTTPS origin, service ownership, and access model are not established.

2. No owner-designated production database or attachment volume was backed up, cloned, restored, inspected, or migrated. Target migration-history reconciliation and no-seed migration rehearsal are not done.
3. Target-specific rollback, existing-volume permissions, certificate trust, off-device backup/key recovery, and post-deployment checks are unverified.

4. Exact-head run 40468488249 on 151bfed built and scanned current source-matched images; artifact 12717453020 reports 3 Critical/69 High for the Bookworm candidate and 1 Critical/61 High for operational Trixie. All four Debian restore routes passed, but the image findings remain open and the Bookworm candidate is not production eligible.

5. Head `70ae656` passed the earlier synthetic backup and isolated restore checks, including Attachment metadata owner/uploader/Tenant linkage and matching file SHA-256; that run used a weaker collation assertion and its apparent Trixie/Bookworm-to-Alpine restore compatibility is superseded by the exact-head default-collation probes on `5bcf9f9`, which failed for both sources. Do not treat the older result as migration compatibility evidence. Neither run proves application-level download authorization, production target recovery, or off-device recovery. No off-device remote is configured; host sleep/restart scheduling and off-device delivery/key recovery remain unverified. The manual rehearsal and weekly scheduler cycle on `3d5db3c` remain historical evidence.

6. PR #2 remains OPEN/Draft with REVIEW_REQUIRED. Exact-head push and PR runs 40468488249/40468493268 passed all four jobs, including container verification; an independent GitHub approval is still required before protected-branch integration. No source-matched image is published for deployment.
7. The Owner requested agent-run UAT instead of Owner UAT. Agent UAT passed 90/90; no Owner acceptance is claimed.
## Next executable work

- Keep PR #2 Draft. Continue safe security remediation and read-only target discovery. Do not use the Alpine database candidate for either tested Debian source. Evaluate a separately isolated Debian database candidate and its security findings; keep the operational Trixie stack and volumes unchanged. Prepare exact-target clone backup/restore, no-seed migration, rollback, HTTPS/volume and off-device recovery evidence. Obtain required independent PR approval before integration. Publish/pull images and perform cutover only after the exact target/release is bound and every gate passes. Agent UAT is synthetic evidence, not production verification.

- Manual and one-cycle scheduled backup/restore checks on older source `3d5db3c` remain historical evidence. Do not imply off-device delivery, production target recovery, application-level attachment authorization, or Owner UAT has passed.
- Production remains NO-GO until an actual target is identified and the target-specific backup, migration, rollback, image publication/pull, and deployment authorization gates are satisfied.
